name: Hincmar of Reims
knownFor: Archbishop of Reims in Frankish Gaul who carried on the royal annals from 861 to 882. He fought Prudentius of Troyes over predestination and his own nephew, Hincmar of Laon, over church law.
dates: At work from 849 to 882. In 849 the bishops at Quierzy sent the condemned Gottschalk to him for custody, Nicolás Antonio says. His annals end in 882 No held source gives his birth or death
place: Reims, where he was archbishop; Épernay, beyond the Marne, where he fled in 882

keyWorks.title: Annals of Saint-Bertin, from 861 to 882
keyWorks.about: the royal annals he carried on after Prudentius of Troyes. Georg Waitz says only Hincmar could have told some of what they hold, such as his own flight to Épernay

keyWorks.title: Chapters for the priests of his diocese

keyWorks.title: Life of Saint Remigius
keyWorks.about: his Life of Remigius, an early bishop of Reims, edited by Bruno Krusch

traces: The council of Douzy deposed his nephew Hincmar of Laon in 871, at the request of King Charles. The annals say the synod sent its acts to Rome by Bishop Actard.
Mansi's council volumes print the writings of both Hincmars of 868, which Ludovicus Cellotius first published. Cellotius says the uncle then fought for his nephew against outside force.
His notice of Prudentius's death, in the annals for 861, is the fullest held account of Prudentius's life.
remembered: Georg Waitz calls him deeply versed in church law and in the affairs of his own time.
Bruno Krusch calls him vain and deceitful. He says Hincmar spiced the tales he made up, and that his long sentences choke the breath.
Nicolás Antonio calls his annal on Prudentius a slander.

uncertain: Much of his story is told by his own annals, which take his side in his quarrels. His opponents' words come through his annals and through notes in Mansi's collection.
What happened to his nephew after Douzy. A note in Mansi's collection says the nephew's complaint to Pope John told of exile, chains and blinding. The held lines do not say who blinded him.
His part in the Gottschalk entry of 849. Georg Waitz reports the abbé Lebeuf's view that Hincmar reworked it in Prudentius's part of the annals.
His birth and death. No held source gives either. His annals stop in 882.
